statement: The variance of a random variable $X$ is defined as the expected value of the squared deviation from the mean of $X$: $\operatorname{Var}(X) = \operatorname{E}\left[{\left(X - \operatorname{E}[X]\right)}^2\right]$.

symbols.meaning: variance of the random variable X
expected value (mean) of the random variable X

properties.why: the variance of $X$ is equal to the mean of the square of $X$ minus the square of the mean of $X$
the variance of a constant is zero
variance is zero if and only if the random variable is almost surely a constant
law of total variance decomposition into expected conditional variance and variance of conditional expectation

assumptions.assumption: The first and second moments of the random variable exist and are finite
assumptions.breaks_when: The distribution has undefined or infinite moments, such as the Cauchy distribution or a Pareto distribution with index $1 < k \le 2$

failure_modes.signature: Loss of numerical precision or non-positive variance estimate in floating-point arithmetic
failure_modes.cause: Computing variance via $\operatorname{E}[X^2] - \operatorname{E}[X]^2$ when the two terms are close in magnitude
The distribution has heavy tails such that the second moment is infinite
